policy: This manifest is the single source of truth for which Xiranite nodes survive the Rust/Tauri rewrite. A node covered by a more specialized standalone project is not re-implemented and gets no node crate. Nodes listed as hold-unmigrated must stay in xiranite.build.toml nodes.disabled and must not be deleted or rewritten this round. Per ADR-0073 every retain-rewrite node carries hostRequirements: the non-empty array of host-service tiers (pure-logic | file-io | recursive-enumeration | external-process | network | os-native | no-host-free-answer, spelled by packages/tauri-migrate/src/node-feasibility.ts) that the AST dependency audit measured, never a verdict taken from the node name. Produce it with bun run audit:node-feasibility, then write it into this file with bun run audit:target-node-manifest -- --apply-host-requirements; hand-typed tier lists are forbidden (ADR-0067). null means no verdict is carried: for a retained node that is unaudited work (a warning, and --strict fails on it), and it is the required value for removed, drop-to-standalone and hold-unmigrated records, which owe no native crate this round. An empty array is never valid, because pure-logic is the analyzer's residual and always stands alone. schemaVersion 2 is this shape; version 1 carried the retired wasmFeasibility string. bun run audit:target-node-manifest fails when this file, xiranite.build.toml and packages/nodes drift apart.

maxLiveBytes: 16777216 = the value five of the six already-ceilinged retained nodes carry (classq/linedup/samea/timeu; 256 wasm pages x 64 KiB before the Extism tree was retired). sleept never had a plugins/<id>/manifest.toml (git log --all -- plugins/sleept/manifest.toml is empty), so the floor was measured instead on 2026-10-06 with target/debug/quickjs-run on this node's own bundle: loading the 121 KiB bundle is refused at 917504 and completes at 1048576, and a full countdown run fits inside 1 MiB. The largest input the node can ever hold is one proc.exec stdout, which the host itself caps at MAX_PROCESS_OUTPUT_BYTES = 1048576, so 16 MiB is at least 3x the worst measured case and is not a limit that was widened to make a gate pass.

runDeadlineMs: 86400000 = 24 h, one hour above the node's own declared timer bound (packages/nodes/sleept/src/interaction.ts:82 caps countdown hours at 23, so the longest countdown is 23:59:59). It exists because a run of this node is mostly waiting and the executor's default would stop it mid-wait: DEFAULT_RUN_DEADLINE is 120 s (crates/quickjs-realm/src/jobs.rs:49) and nobody chose that for a timer. 24 h also bounds the one input that is otherwise open-ended -- netspeed/cpu maxWaitSeconds, where the word list itself spells 0 as 'unlimited' (interaction.ts:108 with previewWait) -- so a forgotten monitor holds one blocking thread for a day, not forever. Enforcement granularity is fine: clock.sleep answers within MAX_SLEEP_MS_PER_CALL = 1000 ms, so the deadline is re-read at least once a second while waiting.
